## [0.23.0] - 2026-10-19

### Security

- **Encrypted files are a core feature, and their text stays encrypted everywhere Editora writes.** Opening a
  `.gpg`, `.pgp` or `.asc` encrypted file decrypts it with GnuPG (the `gpg` you have installed, on this machine),
  and saving encrypts it again for the same people, in the same format. A save that cannot be encrypted (a
  recipient's public key missing, GnuPG failing) writes nothing and says why in a banner. While an encrypted
  file is open, its text gets no crash-recovery copy and no Local History, bookmarks and breakpoints keep only
  line numbers, no personal notes can be added, language servers do not read it (a setting turns them on),
  agents, MCP clients and AI actions are refused, and diagrams are not rendered through temporary files. Save
  As to a plain name, export, print and external tools ask first. Settings schema 136.
- **Plugins: consent belongs to a plugin's folder and to what you were shown.** A plugin's id must be its folder's
  name (a folder that copies another plugin's id is listed with an error and never loads), and plugins.json stores
  a fingerprint of the disclosure with each consent: a plugin whose code, commands or chords changed since does not
  load until you enable it again. Entries of plugins whose folder is gone are dropped at start. plugins.json
  schema 2 carries existing consents over.
- **Plugins: nothing is replaced before you agree.** An install is unpacked beside the plugins and put in place only
  on Enable; a registry archive must be the plugin and version its entry names; installing a different plugin
  under an installed plugin's id asks "Replace A with B?" first. Remove deletes the row you clicked.
- **The plugin consent dialog cannot be forged.** Manifest text is escaped (line breaks, control and bidi
  characters are shown, not obeyed) and capped, the capability list scrolls in a fixed box, and it lists the main
  class and every jar, each command's exact argv and folder, and what each chord replaces. A plugin whose
  plugin.json cannot be read can no longer be ticked.
- **MCP clients cannot switch plugins on, change the signed-registry requirement, install or remove plugins, or
  trust a folder.** The registry URL setter refuses anything but https for every caller.

- **AI API keys are kept in the system keychain** (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, the Secret Service on
  Linux). Keys in settings.json move there on first start, and Settings → AI Actions says where each key is. Where no
  keychain answers, keys stay in settings.json and the page says so. Keys in the keychain are never exported.
- **Export Configuration never includes a password or token stored in the Settings Sync repository URL**, and
  the Sync page offers to remove one stored there before the URL check existed.
- **Switching the AI provider no longer sends one provider's API key to another provider's server.** Anthropic
  and the OpenAI-compatible provider shared one endpoint and model, so after a switch to Anthropic the Anthropic
  key went to the OpenAI-compatible server set up before (and the other way round), within seconds and again on
  every Settings open. The OpenAI-compatible provider now has its own endpoint, model and inline-completion model.
  Settings schema 127 moves an existing OpenAI-compatible endpoint and models to the new fields.
- **Export Configuration leaves the AI API keys out** by default. The export dialog has an "Include AI API keys"
  checkbox, and the Advanced page and the status line say when they were left out.
- **The Settings Sync repository field refuses a URL with a password or token in it** (`https://user:TOKEN@…`)
  and suggests a credential helper (`gh auth setup-git`) or SSH, so the token is not stored in settings.json, the
  export or the clone.

### Added

- **Kotlin: JetBrains' Kotlin LSP, Run and Debug.** Kotlin's language server is now JetBrains' Kotlin LSP: one
  click installs a pinned release (about 370 MB with its own Java runtime, which Editora says before it starts),
  and it imports the Gradle build for completion, navigation and diagnostics. A configured command is kept, so
  fwcd's kotlin-language-server still works. Run File, the gutter ▶ and a new Kotlin run configuration run a
  `.kts` script with `kotlinc -script`, and compile a `.kt` file with a top-level `main` into a cached jar that runs
  with `java -jar` on the Settings JDK (compiled again only when the file changes); the Run window shows the Kotlin
  and Java versions. Debug stops at breakpoints in programs, scripts and lambdas through Editora's own debugger,
  names frames as Kotlin does (`Hello.main { lambda }`), and steps over the standard library and coroutines
  machinery. Debug via Build Tool and Attach to JVM work from a Kotlin file too.
- **Groovy: language server, Run and Debug.** Groovy files get completion, diagnostics, outline, rename and
  formatting from the gvy language server, installed in one click (a pinned jar, run on the JDK chosen in Settings).
  Run File, the gutter ▶ and a new Groovy script run configuration run a script with `groovy` on that JDK, and the
  Run window shows the Groovy and Java versions. Debug stops at breakpoints in scripts, classes and closures, steps
  over Groovy's own runtime, shows locals and fields, and stops on uncaught exceptions — through a new debugger
  built into Editora, so there is nothing else to install. Settings schema 138.
- **Run File runs Node.js scripts.** A `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.ts`, `.mts` or `.cts` file, or a script with a
  `node` (or `deno`, `bun`, `tsx`) shebang, gets a gutter ▶ and runs in the Run console under the Node.js Editora
  resolves (the Node.js setting, the project's `.nvmrc`/`.node-version`, else `node` on PATH), from its package
  folder, with `--enable-source-maps` and colours on. TypeScript runs on plain Node 22.18+; an older Node says so.
  The ▶ of a test file (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, `test/`, `__tests__/`) runs `node --test` into Test Results, with
  Rerun Failed and Rerun This Test. Run configurations gain a **Node.js script** type (script, Node.js arguments,
  interpreter, arguments, environment).
- **One Node.js for everything.** Settings → Debugging → JavaScript has a **Node.js** field used by Run, run
  configurations, Debug, npm scripts, the TypeScript language server and (when its own field is blank) HTTP
  response handlers. Left blank, Editora uses the version a project's `.nvmrc` or `.node-version` names when nvm has
  it, else `node` on PATH. Doctor has one **Node.js** row saying which Node runs and why.
- **Debugging JavaScript and TypeScript.** `.ts`, `.mts` and `.cts` files can be debugged on Node 22.18+, and a
  breakpoint in a compiled project's `.ts` source stops there through source maps. **Debug ▸ Attach** on a JS/TS file
  connects to a Node started with `--inspect`. **Debug Test at Caret** runs the node:test test at the caret. Node.js
  and npm run configurations can be debugged, started the way Run starts them.
- **TypeScript server settings:** **Download type definitions automatically** (off), and inlay hints and code
  lenses now work for JavaScript and TypeScript.
- **A Node.js Script template** (New ▸ Scripts ▸ Node.js), and an npm icon on `package.json`, `package-lock.json`
  and `.npmrc`.
- **Test Results reads node:test's default output**, so `"test": "node --test"` fills the tree without a TAP
  reporter flag, and node:test results can be rerun one by one or failed-only.
- **Encrypted files** (Tools ▸ Encryption; [ADR 0017](docs/decisions/0017-encrypted-files.md)). An encrypted
  file opens as the text inside it, in that text's language (`notes.md.gpg` is Markdown), with a lock on its tab
  and an "Encrypted · 2" item in the status bar that opens the details: who can read it (you, verified or not),
  its format, its signature.
  - **Locked tabs** instead of hex or errors: a cancelled prompt, a file none of your keys opens, or GnuPG not
    installed shows what happened and the next step. Restored tabs stay locked until you decrypt them, so
    startup never asks for a run of passphrases.
  - **Encrypt File…** (also on the Project tree and tab menus, and Save As to a `.gpg`/`.asc` name) opens a
    recipient picker: searchable, several people at once or a passphrase instead, your own key included by
    default, unverified keys warned about with their fingerprint, expired and sign-only keys shown with the
    reason. It can write the folder's `.gpg-id` (the `pass` format) so new files there get the same people.
    The plain original stays until you move it to the trash from the banner.
  - **Change Recipients…** (applied on the next save), **Remove Encryption…**, **Lock File**, **Decrypt to
    File…**, **Encrypt Selection…** and **Decrypt Block at Caret** (an armored message pasted into a note opens
    in a read-only card), **Import Public Key…** (and an opened `.asc` key offers it), **Clear-Sign**, **Sign
    File (Detached)** and **Verify Signature**.
  - Passphrases go to gpg-agent's own prompt; when it cannot show one (a terminal pinentry), Editora asks and
    hands the passphrase straight to GnuPG. A passphrase-only file is asked once and saves without asking again.
  - Settings ▸ Encryption (gpg path, always include my key, who asks for passphrases, language servers) and two
    Doctor rows (GnuPG, passphrase prompt). Samples in `samples/encrypted/` (passphrase `editora`).
- **Clojure: language server, build tools, Run and Debug.** Clojure, ClojureScript and EDN files get completion,
  diagnostics (clj-kondo's), navigation, rename and formatting from clojure-lsp, installed in one click (a pinned
  native binary, checked by its SHA-256) or found on PATH. A `deps.edn`, `project.clj` or `bb.edn` project gets a
  Clojure CLI, Leiningen or Babashka toolbar button: the CLI's runnable aliases (`-M:test`, `-X:build`,
  `-T:build`), Leiningen's common tasks, a `bb.edn`'s tasks. Run File, the gutter ▶ (on `(defn -main`, else the
  top of a script) and a new Clojure script run configuration run a namespace with `clojure -M -m` in its
  project, through `lein run` in a Leiningen project, a script with `clojure -M`, and a Babashka script with
  `bb`; an uncaught exception's whole trace is printed (not left in a temporary file), and its frames are links.
  Debug stops at breakpoints in a namespace's functions or a script's top-level forms, under the Clojure CLI or
  Leiningen, with locals kept visible and frames named as Clojure names them (`my-app.core/greet`); Babashka,
  a native program, cannot be debugged and says so. Settings schema 139.
- **Scala: Metals, sbt, Mill, Scala CLI, Run and Debug.** Scala files get completion, diagnostics, navigation,
  rename and formatting from Metals 1.6.9, installed in one click (a pinned coursier resolves it into Editora's
  folder; it runs on the JDK chosen in Settings). Language servers' questions are now asked — Metals' "Import
  build?" among them — and Metals' input boxes, pick lists and status items work. sbt (`build.sbt`), Mill
  (`build.mill`, `build.sc`) and Scala CLI (`project.scala`) projects get a toolbar button, actions popup and
  console like Gradle's, with each sbt subproject's or Mill module's tasks loaded on demand. Run File and the
  gutter ▶ (on an `@main def`, an `object … extends App`, a `def main`, or a `.sc` script) run a file of an sbt or
  Mill build through it (`sbt "runMain …"`, `./mill <module>.runMain …`) and any other file with Scala CLI, with
  the Scala CLI and Scala versions in the Run window; a new Scala run configuration runs files with Scala CLI.
  Debug uses Metals' debug adapter for a file of a build, and Editora's own debugger over Scala CLI for a script,
  stepping over the standard library. Settings schema 140.
- **Scala and Clojure editing.** `.scala`, `.sc`, `.sbt`, `.mill` and `.clj`, `.cljs`, `.cljc`, `.cljx`, `.edn`, `.bb`
  files are highlighted (grammars from tm-grammars 1.32.22), as are `#!` scripts run by `scala`, `scala-cli`,
  `kotlin`, `clojure`, `clj` or `bb` and files with a `scala`/`clojure` modeline. Comment toggling (`;;` in Clojure),
  folding (Scala 3's indentation blocks through their `end` marker; every multi-line Clojure form), Lisp indentation
  (to the first argument, two spaces for a body form), Go to Symbol without a language server, a Structure outline,
  snippets, brand file icons, and New ▸ Scala, Scala CLI script, Clojure and Babashka script. Groovy gets its own
  icon and a server-free symbol index too, and stack-trace lines from Kotlin, Groovy, Scala and Clojure code are
  links (including Clojure's `at my-app.core/f (core.clj:4)`).
- **`--disable-plugins`** starts Editora with no plugin loaded for the session: the way out of a plugin that hangs or
  breaks startup. Settings and Doctor say when it is on.
- **Doctor → Plugins** lists what runs and every plugin that failed to load or start, started slowly, or changed
  since it was enabled.
- **Plugin chords per keymap**: a manifest's `keymaps` gives chords for one keymap (`emacs`, `cua`, …) in place of
  `keymap`.
- **Plugins: Restart now** on a Settings row whose change waits for a restart, and status and errors shown on the
  Plugins page itself.

- **Settings shows what you changed.** A row whose value differs from the default carries a marker, the sidebar counts
  them per page, each row has **Reset to default**, and the **Modified** toggle (or `@modified` in the search) lists
  only the changed settings.
- **Project settings.** In a project window, Settings has a **User | Project** switch. A project's
  `.editora/settings.json` can set indentation, tab size, rulers, wrap, trimming trailing whitespace, the final
  newline, the spelling dictionary, build commands, debugger paths and language servers. The values apply in that
  project's windows once the folder is trusted; `.editorconfig` still wins where it sets something. Rows say when a
  project sets or overrides them.
- **Import Configuration…** (Settings → Advanced, or *Configuration: Import from Zip*) reads a zip made by Export
  Configuration. It shows each part and what it would replace, lets you untick parts, backs up the current
  configuration to `backups/` first, applies what it can at once and offers a restart for the rest. It refuses a zip
  that is not an export, unsafe entry names and oversized entries.
- **Restart Now.** Settings that apply at startup (language, merged title bar, plugins) show "Restart Editora to apply
  N changes." with **Restart Now** (also *Application: Restart*), which quits the usual way and starts Editora again.
- **Settings → Sync shows a status pill:** green *Connected* (with when it last synced), amber *Not connected* (not set
  up, turned off, or offline and retrying) and red *Sync failing* (it needs you), with the reason under it.
- **Each Settings page links to its documentation** with a **?** beside the title.
- **File Watching** row in the Doctor: says when the system has no file watcher to give and Editora checks folders by
  polling instead.
- **Deployments: develop locally, run on another machine.** A run configuration's new **Run on** setting names a
  deployment — an SSH host and a folder there. Before the run, Editora copies what changed in the project to
  that folder over the connection it already uses for remote folders (one compressed stream; no rsync or ssh
  needed on this machine), then runs the before-launch step and the program there, with the host's tools.
  - Only files whose contents changed are sent; a branch switch that only touched times sends nothing.
  - Files Editora put on the host and the project no longer has are removed; nothing else on the host is ever
    removed. A file changed on the host since it was sent is asked about, a first deploy into a folder with other
    files asks first, and `/`, system folders and the home folder are refused.
  - Java builds on the host with its Maven or Gradle. Debug starts the program on the host and attaches the
    debugger here through a tunnel; breakpoints are the local files'.
  - Run → Deployment: Deploy Now, Compare with Deployed, Open Terminal in Deployment, Edit Deployments. A
    deployment can also upload a file when it is saved. Deployments are exported and imported with the run
    configurations.
- **A Terminal tool window**: shells on this machine, in tabs, inside Editora. Open it with Tool Window:
  Terminal (Alt+F12 in the IntelliJ keymap, Ctrl+` in VS Code, CUA and Sublime). It starts in the project's
  folder; Terminal: New Terminal adds a tab.
  - A focused terminal owns the keyboard: Ctrl+C interrupts, Ctrl+W deletes a word, Escape reaches vim. The
    tool windows, the command palette and Search Everywhere still reach Editora, but only on keys a shell does
    not use: a plain Ctrl+letter, Alt+letter, Alt+digit or F-key always goes to the shell, whatever the keymap
    binds to it (IntelliJ's Ctrl+K, VS Code's Ctrl+B and F1). The terminal's own commands and the Emacs
    keymap's M-x pass on any key, and a key typed into Settings → Terminal → Commands that reach Editora (say
    `M-1`) passes too. Every Cmd shortcut on macOS reaches Editora. Copy and Paste are Ctrl+Shift+C/V
    (Cmd+C/V on macOS), shown in the terminal's menu. Shift+Escape returns to the editor and leaves the
    terminal open; Shift+PageUp/PageDown/Home/End scroll the history.
  - On macOS, Option types the characters your keyboard layout puts on it (@ [ ] { } on many layouts);
    Settings → Terminal → "Option key as Meta" makes it readline's Meta instead. Alt is Meta on Linux and
    Windows.
  - Tabs can be renamed, moved (drag, Ctrl+Shift+PageUp/PageDown, or the tab's menu) and closed from a tab
    menu; Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown switch between them, and tabs with the same title are numbered. A bell in a
    tab out of sight marks it.
  - The terminal is in the Window menu (Terminal, New Terminal) and the File menu (Open Terminal Here); the
    Emacs keymap opens it with M-0. It follows the editor's text zoom. It hides when its last shell exits.
  - Pasting several lines into a program that would run each at once (sh, a REPL) asks first; a paste can no
    longer carry control characters or end bash's bracketed paste early.
  - Closing a window or quitting asks when terminals are running programs, in one question.
  - Its colours follow the editor theme: the keyword colour is its red, the number colour its blue, and so on.
    Its font is the editor's.
  - Build Output's stripe icon is now the tools glyph; the terminal glyph is the Terminal's.
  - Closing a terminal that is running a program asks first.
  - **Open Terminal Here** (tab menu, Project tree, breadcrumb, command) opens a tab there instead of the
    system's terminal; Settings → Terminal → "Open Terminal Here uses the system terminal" brings the old
    behaviour back.
  - Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on macOS) a `path:line:col` in the output to open the file at that place, or a URL
    to open it in the browser.
  - Settings → Terminal: the shell, text size, cursor, bell, scrollback, and which commands reach Editora.
  - **In a remote project, terminals run on the host**: a real terminal (vim, htop and resizing work) over the
    project's own SSH connection, starting in the project's folder. Its tab is labelled with the host. If the
    connection drops, the tab keeps its text and offers Reconnect.
  - **A folder whose tools run in a dev container or a WSL distribution gets its terminal there too**: a login
    shell in the container (`docker`/`podman exec -it`) or the distribution (`wsl.exe`), in the folder, labelled
    with the container's or distribution's name. Closing the terminal ends the shell inside.
  - **Shell integration** (bash and zsh, on this machine and on hosts, containers and WSL): the terminal knows
    the shell's folder, so relative paths in the output open the right file and **New Terminal Here** opens a
    tab where the shell is. Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down (Cmd+Up/Down on macOS) jump between prompts, and **Copy Last
    Command Output** copies what the last command printed. Closing a remote terminal that is running a program
    asks first. Settings → Terminal → Shell integration turns it off.
  - **Find in the terminal** (Ctrl+Shift+F, Cmd+F on macOS, or Terminal: Find) highlights every match in the
    scrollback; Enter goes to older ones.
  - **OSC 8 hyperlinks** (`ls --hyperlink`, gcc, git and other tools that mark links) open with a Ctrl/Cmd
    click; hovering one whose text is not its address shows the address.
  - **Type-ahead** shows what you type at once over a slow SSH connection, dimmed until the shell echoes it.
    It starts only when echoes take over 100 ms (Settings → Terminal → Type-ahead).
  - **Run in a Terminal tab**: a run configuration's Console option runs its program in the Terminal (programs
    that draw on the screen or read single keys), locally or on the project's host. The tab stays when it
    ends, with the exit code; closing it while the program runs asks first. Run's Stop button and stripe
    follow it, the next run of the same configuration reuses its tab, the configuration's variables win over
    the login profile's, and a missing working folder fails the run as in the console.
  - **Debug in a Terminal tab**: Settings → Debugging → Java → "Run the program in a Terminal tab instead" does the same
    for a debugged Java or Python program.
  - A terminal on a host or in a container opens without freezing the window: its tab says "Connecting to …"
    until the shell is there.
  - The terminal is Termina's (github.com/adriandeleon/Termina), ported.
- **The Run and Debug tool windows say which runtime the program runs under**, in a small chip beside the
  state: `Java 25.0.4 (Temurin)`, `Python 3.13.5`, `Node.js 24.18.1`, `Bash 5.2.37`, `GNU Make 4.4.1`. Hover it
  for the runtime's own version banner and, for Java, the JDK's folder.
  - It asks the very executable the run starts, in the run's folder and environment — so a run configuration's
    JDK, a virtualenv's `python`, a pyenv `.python-version` and a remote host's own runtime are what it reports.
  - The program doesn't wait for the answer: the chip fills in a moment after the launch. It stays after the
    program exits and is replaced by the next run. A runtime it can't ask (a plain `sh`, a compiled binary) and
    an attached debug session show no chip.
- **Settings search ranks its results.** A hit in a setting's title beats one in its description, a whole word
  beats part of a word, and the page with the best row opens; matching rows are tinted. Synonyms find settings
  known by another name (zoom, line endings, encoding, hotkey, colour scheme, soft wrap, gutter), and the search
  also finds commands in the Keymaps list. Ctrl+F (⌘F) focuses the search, typing on the sidebar starts one, and the
  sidebar scrolls to the page that opens.
- **Saving `settings.json` in an Editora tab applies it** in every window, and the Advanced page lists anything in
  the file that was ignored or changed on load (unknown keys, wrong types, out-of-range values).
- **Restore from Backup…** on the Advanced page brings back settings from a backup that Reset to Defaults wrote.
- **AI Actions: Test connection.** Opening Settings no longer sends a request to the AI provider. The connection
  is checked while the AI Actions page is shown, a result is reused for three minutes, and Test connection checks
  again.
- **Keymaps:** **Remove** (and the Delete key) unbinds a command. The filter finds words in any order, and a query
  that reads as a chord (Ctrl+Shift+S, C-S-s, ⇧⌘S, Ctrl+K Ctrl+W) lists the commands on that chord.
- **Tool Windows page:** rows are grouped Left / Right / Bottom in stripe order, and **Restore Default Layout** puts
  the tool windows back where they start.
- **Editor theme "Automatic"** follows the app theme again after you picked an editor theme.
- **Remote page:** **Connect…** opens the Connect form for the selected site; host, port and user are checked as
  you type; a missing key file is flagged.
- **MCP page:** shows whether the server runs and where, with **Copy Endpoint Command** and **New Token**.
- **Debugging page:** an **Install…** button on each adapter card.
- **Web page:** choose the browser HTML preview opens in; a Found / Not found row for Node.js.
- **LSP page:** a card says when the project's `.editora/settings.json` overrides its server command.
- **Appearance:** while text zoom is not 100% a row says so, with Reset zoom, and the live preview uses the zoomed
  size. A "Your own themes" row opens the themes folder and reloads themes.
- **Settings Sync:** Cancel while Connect looks at the repository; the page says what is not synced.
- **23 more bundled file templates** (New File From Template), 32 in all:
  - **Code:** JUnit 5 Test (in the folder's package), Java Shebang Script (an extensionless file the `java`
    launcher runs directly), pytest Test Module, and a Node.js TypeScript Project (module, `node:test` test,
    `tsconfig.json`, README).
  - **Files Editora previews or runs:** Typst Document, Typst Document + Template (`template.typ` plus a document
    that imports it), Mermaid Diagram, Markwhen Timeline, and HTTP Requests + Environments (a `.http` file with
    `@assert`/`@capture` checks plus dev/prod `http-client.env.json` and `http-client.private.env.json`).
  - **Containers:** Dockerfile (Java), a multi-stage Maven build that runs the jar on a JRE as a non-root user,
    and the same with a `compose.yaml` and a `.dockerignore`.
  - **Writing:** README, Changelog (Keep a Changelog), Architecture Decision Record, Blog Post (YAML front matter,
    dated file name) and Meeting Notes.
  - **Project files:** License: MIT (this year and your author name), License: Apache 2.0 (verbatim), `.gitignore`
    for Java, Python and Node, `.editorconfig`, and GitHub Issue + PR Templates under `.github/`.
  - The multi-file ones are also offered by New Project From Template.
- **Remote: logins ask what they need, while they run.** The connect form no longer has a Secret field. A
  password, a key's passphrase, and a server's own questions — a 2FA or one-time code, a Duo answer — are asked
  for in a login dialog when the server or the key needs them, as `ssh` does. A wrong answer is asked for again;
  a cancelled passphrase skips that key and the login goes on.
  - Password logins no longer try your default SSH keys first, and a key login uses only that key.
  - A failed connect says why: the host could not be reached, did not answer, its host key has changed (with
    the `ssh-keygen -R` line to remove the old entry), or the login was refused. Cancelling only says so in the
    status bar.
- **Remote: SSH agent.** An Automatic login uses the keys your SSH agent holds — `ssh-agent`, 1Password,
  Secretive, gpg-agent, or Windows' OpenSSH agent — before any key file, so a key on a security key (FIDO) or a
  smartcard, or one kept in a password manager, logs in. `IdentityAgent` in your SSH config chooses the agent
  (`none` turns it off). Waiting for a security key's touch does not time the login out. The agent is never
  forwarded to the server.
- **Remote: `~/.ssh/config`.** The connect form offers the hosts your SSH config names, and for the host you
  type shows where it really goes (HostName, ProxyJump, IdentityFile) and fills in its User and Port. Logging
  in follows the config as `ssh` does: its `IdentityFile` keys, `IdentitiesOnly`, and `ProxyJump` through a
  jump host. "Default SSH keys" is now **Automatic (like ssh)**: the agent's keys, then the config's, then
  your default ones. `Include` lines are followed, globs too (`Include conf.d/*`, on Windows as well).
  `ProxyCommand` is not supported.
- **Python: one interpreter for Run, Debug and code intelligence.** Editora now finds a project's own Python: an
  activated environment (`$VIRTUAL_ENV`, `$CONDA_PREFIX`), else a `.venv`/`venv`/`env` folder in the project, else
  Settings → Debugging → Python interpreter, else the system Python (`py -3` on Windows, never the Microsoft Store
  stub). Run, run configurations, Debug, Pyright, Doctor and the formatter all use the same answer.
  - A **status-bar item** on Python files shows the interpreter and why (`Python 3.13.5 (.venv)`); click it (or
    `Python: Select Interpreter`) to pick one of the project's environments, a Python on PATH, or any file, per
    project. "Detect automatically" goes back to the rules above.
  - Pyright is told the interpreter, so a venv's packages resolve without a `pyrightconfig.json`.
  - On SSH hosts, WSL and containers the project's venv is found on that machine; a new **`python` host tool**
    sets the host's Python.
- **Python tests: a pytest runner.** Test files (`test_*.py`, `*_test.py`) get a gutter ▶ on every test function,
  class and method and one for the whole file; results fill the Test Results window, with Rerun, Rerun Failed and
  run-one-row. It uses pytest when the interpreter has it, else `unittest` for `TestCase` tests, else says how to
  install pytest. **Debug Test** works from a test line and from a Test Results row.
- **Python: Format Document runs Ruff or Black** (the project venv's first, then PATH), also with language
  servers off. Doctor shows which one it will use.
- **Python run configurations:** an **Interpreter** and **Interpreter options** field, and a new **Python module**
  type that runs `python -m <name>`.
- **Debugging:** a **hit count** for breakpoints (Edit Breakpoint), an **exception breakpoint picker** that lists what
  the debugger offers (Python: raised, uncaught, user-uncaught), **Debug File** next to Run File in the editor's
  menu, and the exit code at the end of a Python debug session.
- **Python editing:** folding by indentation (so sticky scroll pins Python scopes), and highlighting for pip
  requirements files.
- **"Turn on Python code intelligence?"** — a one-time offer when the first Python file opens while language
  servers are off.
- **Java debugging: hot code replace.** Saving a `.java` file during a Java debug session rebuilds it with the
  Java language server and loads the new code into the running program. The Debug console says which classes
  changed, or why they could not be (adding a method or field still needs a restart). Settings → Debugging →
  "Apply code changes to a running Java program": automatically (default), on command only, or off; and
  **Debug: Apply Code Changes**.
- **Java debugging: Restart Frame** (call-stack right-click menu and a command) and **Smart Step Into…** (pick
  which call on the line to step into).
- **Debug: Breakpoints…** lists every breakpoint: Enter jumps to it, Alt+E enables or disables it, Alt+D removes it,
  Alt+M mutes them all. Also **Mute Breakpoints**, **Enable/Disable Breakpoint** at the caret, and a right-click
  menu on a breakpoint glyph (Edit…, Enable/Disable, Remove, Breakpoints…).
- **Completion while debugging.** Ctrl+Space, or typing `.`, lists what the debugger can complete in the Debug
  console's evaluate field, the watch prompt and a breakpoint's condition and log message (while the program is
  paused).
- **The value popup unfolds.** Hovering a variable, or Show Value at Caret, shows an object, array or collection as a
  tree (big arrays a page at a time), with Copy Value and Add to Watches; arrow keys, Enter and Shift+Enter work it
  from the keyboard.
- **Exception breakpoints: Caught and Uncaught** are two toggles, checked in the Run menu and shown in the Debug
  window, kept per project. Settings → Debugging can limit them to some exception classes.
- **Java step filters and static fields.** Step Into skips JDK classes and synthetic methods, and a class's static
  fields show among the variables; both are on by default and can be turned off in Settings → Debugging.
- **Show Value at Caret** (keyboard), **Copy Value**, **Copy Name** and **Add to Watches** (filled in from the
  selected variable) in the Variables tree; Up/Down history in the evaluate field.
- **Debugger keys in every keymap.** CUA and Sublime get VS Code's F-keys (F5, Shift+F5, Ctrl+Shift+F5, F6, F9,
  F10, F11 = Step Into while paused and Full Screen otherwise, Shift+F11); IntelliJ, VS Code and Emacs gain the
  missing ones. The Run menu lists every debugger action, and the editor's right-click menu has Toggle/Edit
  Breakpoint, and while paused Run to Cursor, Show Value and Add to Watches.
- **JDK and library frames show their source** (read-only) when you step into them or click them.

- **HTTP Client: Run All lists every request.** After Run All the response view used to show one response and a
  line like "Run All: 3 of 10 failed". Now a results list sits above the tabs: a title ("Run All · 3 of 10 failed ·
  4.1 s"), then one row per request in run order with its status, name, method and path, time, and tests (`✗ 2/3`
  in red when one failed). The first failure is selected and shown; selecting another row shows that response in
  the tabs. **Only failures** hides the rest, the chevron collapses the list, and the list scrolls on its own so
  the tabs keep their room. Enter or a double-click goes to the request in the editor; right-click a row to run it
  again or copy it as cURL. A cancelled Run All lists the requests that finished. The list stays until the next run
  or Clear.

- **HTTP Client: results on the request lines.** After a request in a `.http` file runs, its method/URL line shows
  how it went, in muted text: `200 OK · 83 ms · ✗ 1 of 3 tests`, `404 Not Found · 1 ms`, `Connection refused`. The
  status is in the outcome's colour, failed tests are red, and the request's ▶ takes the colour too (amber for a
  4xx, red for a 5xx, a failure or failed tests).
  - Click the result to show that response in the response view; hover it to see when it ran.
  - The results come from the response history, so they are back when the file is reopened, and Clear removes them.
    A request whose line you edit loses its result.
  - The text is not part of the file: it is never copied, searched, saved or undone.
  - Settings → Web → HTTP Client → **Show results after each request line** (on), or `HTTP: Toggle Results After
    Request Lines`.
- **Run Configurations → Main class has a Browse… button**: pick the `.java` file and the fully qualified class
  name is filled in (`src/main/java/test/App.java` → `test.App`), from the file's `main` method or else its
  package and name. A configuration still called "New Configuration" is renamed after the class.

### Removed

- **The GnuPG registry plugin (`gpg-tools`)**: GnuPG is built in now. An installed copy is removed at startup
  (its gpg path and last recipient are kept), and it can no longer be installed.

### Changed

- **What a session runs is what it started with.** Every window applies the plugins that loaded at launch; an
  install, update, enable, disable or removal takes effect at the next start, as the Settings page says. An update
  or removal of a running plugin is applied at the next start before anything loads (Windows cannot replace an
  open jar), and a declined update keeps the installed version, enabled.
- **Plugin commands and tool windows are always in the plugin's namespace** (`plugin.<id>.…`), so a plugin can no
  longer replace a built-in command; an untitled one shows the plugin's name, and tool-window toggles read
  "Tool Window: …".
- **`activeEditor()` stays on the buffer it was asked for**: a plugin that finishes on a worker writes into the
  file it started on, never the tab in front by then (format-runner overwrote another file). Plugin API reads off
  the JavaFX thread throw; writes are handed to it.
- **Plugin feedback is visible and translated**: start and main-class failures go to the Message Log and the
  Settings row, a failed start's commands, chords and segments are taken back, failing plugin commands name the
  plugin, declared commands show their output, and install and registry errors are sentences in your language in
  a dialog titled "Plugins".
- **Settings → Plugins**: installed plugins come first, Browse comes back to Settings when its picker closes,
  Browse and Install from file are greyed while plugins are off (Simple mode says it is the reason), Remove names
  the plugin and its saved data, and "Require signed plugins" is now "Require a signed registry".
- **Export Configuration asks before including the data plugins saved**, and never includes the installer's
  staging folders.
- **The example plugin uses chords that are free in every keymap** (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+E / Y).

- **Changing tab size or another view setting with many files open is about nine times faster**; tabs that are not
  shown catch up when you show them.
- **Codex has its own model setting** instead of sharing Anthropic's.
- **Sync Now can be cancelled** until it starts writing files on this computer.
- **Plugin load errors are translated**; the parser's own text is in the tooltip.
- **View: Toggle Word Wrap** changes the project's value in a trusted project that sets wrap. The Doctor's build and
  debug rows and Markdown lint's tab handling use the project's values too. The trust command is named *Project: Trust
  This Project's Settings*.
- **Installing the Java language server gets Eclipse JDT LS 1.62.0** (was 1.60.0): Java 27 support,
  per-parameter signature help, a quick fix to change a field's access modifier, and Javadoc rendering fixes. An
  existing install keeps its version until it is installed again.
- **Doctor tells the truth about a healthy machine and puts problems first.** A missing tool is red only when
  something in the window needs it: a file of that language is open, the project has its marker file
  (`pom.xml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`…), or you set its command. Everything else is a neutral
  "Not installed" that keeps its Install… button and is not counted. Turning LSP on used to show about fifteen
  red rows for languages never opened.
  - Problems and warnings move to a "Needs attention" group at the top; a section that is all OK folds to one
    line, and the not-installed tools of a section fold together. The summary counts in words ("1 problem")
    and its counts jump to the group.
  - Rows show a status pill like the Settings pages, the tool with its command under it, and the version or
    path in one column. Settings… sits on every row (shown on hover where nothing is wrong); a turned-off
    feature has **Turn on**; the Python formatter has **How to install**; right-click copies a row or its path,
    or reveals the path.
  - **Copy Report** puts a plain-text report (Editora version, OS, Java, every row) on the clipboard.
  - Rows update in place, so the keyboard focus no longer jumps to the toolbar as each result arrives.
    Refresh and Install… keep the last results on screen while checking again, the summary shows the progress,
    the header says when the check ran, and an install's button reads "Installing…".
  - Tips match the problem: Java debugging with LSP off offers Turn on (not Install…), a server with no command
    says so, and debugpy is named as a Python module with its `pip install` line.
  - Build-tool rows check the command set in Settings or the project's wrapper, not just `mvn`/`go`/… on PATH.
  - Graphviz and PlantUML show their versions (`dot -V`, `plantuml -version`).
  - New rows: the AI provider (is a key set), the container engine, and WSL on Windows. New sections:
    Formatting & Linting, HTTP Client, Remote & Containers.
  - In a project on an SSH host, WSL or a container, the header says the rows describe this computer.
  - The message log has an **Open Doctor** button.
- **The Welcome page was reworked** after a UI review:
  - **Recent Projects** are listed above Recent Files, newest first, each opening (or focusing) its project's window. A project
    whose folder is gone is not offered.
  - A recent row keeps the **file name** whole and shortens the folder from its start; a long path no longer
    widens the page or pushes it off-centre. Folders are relative to the project (whose chip already names it)
    or start with `~`; a remote file names its host. Right-click a row to copy its path or remove it.
  - **1–9 open the numbered entries**, and the page focuses the first one when it opens, so Enter opens it.
  - A **Customize** block names the keymap and theme and changes them; with the Emacs keymap it explains the
    `C-`/`M-` notation. On a first run it sits right under Start.
  - **Open File shows its own chord** (Ctrl+O in the VS Code keymap, not Quick Open's Ctrl+P; C-x C-f in Emacs).
  - Text zoom scales the whole layout, so labels and chords no longer clip at 150 %. Links underline on hover and
    keyboard focus only, action rows highlight on hover, "Show 7 more" says what it does, the footer link
    matches the footer, and saved sites no longer repeat their name or print port 22.
  - Doctor moved to a **Help** row with Documentation and What's New (this build's release notes).
- **Closing the last tab leaves a hint in the editor area** (Open File, Open Folder, Command Palette, Welcome
  Page, with their chords) instead of a blank panel, and keeps focus there rather than on the toolbar.
- **Groundwork for an integrated terminal** ([ADR 0014](docs/decisions/0014-integrated-terminal.md)): the
  app now carries JediTerm core (the terminal emulator), pty4j (pseudo-terminals on macOS, Linux and Windows),
  JNA and the Kotlin standard library, about 7.5 MB more in the installed app. Nothing uses them yet apart from
  `editora --check-terminal`, which starts a shell on a pseudo-terminal and says whether it answered.
- **The technical dictionary knows over 900 more terms**: Git (worktree, unstaged, rebasing), editor and UI
  words (submenu, breakpoint, strikethrough, monospace), shell tools (ripgrep, fzf, cwd), Unix and C (inode,
  glibc, malloc, cgroup, ncurses), cryptography (cryptographic, kerberos, keyring), fonts and graphics (harfbuzz,
  colormap, grayscale), the Java toolchain (jlink, jpackage, Temurin), language servers, web, devops and AI names,
  -ed and -ing forms of the words it already had (deserialized, symlinking, canonicalized), and British spellings
  (tokenised, rasterising). It no longer lists "nat", "elt", "os", "io" or "gan", which hid typos of "not",
  "let", "so", "to" and "can". The file is sorted by section and explains what not to add; plurals it listed
  twice are gone, since spell check accepts the plural of any listed word.
- **Debug variables use the editor's syntax colours.** Names, values and types in the Debug tool window's
  variables and watches are coloured like code in the current editor theme — strings, numbers, `true`/`null`/`None`
  and type names — including each element of a list or dict value, instead of the app's status colours.
- **Settings: every external tool row looks and reads the same** — language servers, debug adapters, Mermaid,
  Diagrams, Typst, build tools, Node.js and AI agents show "tool: found (path)" or "tool: not found", then
  Install… or a link. Diagrams links to its install help, and Build Tools says whether the command it would run
  exists.
- **The theme pickers group themes under Light and Dark headings**, with your own themes in a group of their own.
- **Keyboard chips read on every app theme**, whatever the editor theme: the shortcut colour follows the app theme
  everywhere (palette, Welcome, menus, Keymaps), with at least 4.5:1 contrast on all bundled themes.
- **Macros:** the step reorder buttons are labelled Move Up / Move Down and grey out at either end.
- **Python Run:**
  - The script runs in its own folder with the project root and `src/` on `PYTHONPATH`, so package imports work.
  - A saved run configuration writes that folder into Working directory.
  - Output streams as the program prints (`PYTHONUNBUFFERED`) and is UTF-8 on every platform.
  - A specific shebang (`python3.12`, `pypy3`, `uv run --script`) is honoured.
  - **Stop** sends Ctrl-C first, so `finally` blocks and `atexit` handlers run, and the console's first line shows
    the command that ran.
- **Python Debug** runs the program in the same folder, with the same interpreter and `PYTHONPATH` as Run.
  - A program that reads `input()` gets the program console.
  - An uncaught exception stops the debugger, as in VS Code.
  - `multiprocessing` children run instead of waiting for a debugger.
- **Python typing:**
  - `else`, `elif`, `except`, `finally` and `case` line up with their statement as you type the `:`.
  - Enter after `return`, `pass`, `raise`, `break` or `continue` steps out a level.
  - Wrapped statements and open brackets indent as PEP 8 shows.
  - In Python and YAML, Backspace in the indentation removes one level and no longer joins the line above.
- **Python code intelligence:**
  - Unused names are faded and deprecated calls struck through.
  - Go to Definition into the standard library or site-packages stays on the project's server and opens the file
    read-only.
  - Organize Imports works for Python and for any server with a `source.organizeImports` action.
  - Python keeps its server up to 50,000 lines.
  - Untitled Python buffers get it too.
- **Python highlighting:** generics (`def f[T]`, `class C[T]`), `type` aliases, t-strings, `match` used as a name, and
  `0x`/`j` numbers. `__init__` and other methods named like builtins are back in Structure.
- **Python snippets:** Enter after a keyword such as `try` ends the line instead of inserting the `try` snippet; Tab
  still expands it.
- **Python indentation:** a file's indent size is guessed from its statements only, so PEP 8 hanging indents no
  longer make it 8 spaces.
- **Language names:** the status bar and the language picker show readable names ("pip requirements").
- **Quotes:** `f"`, `rb"` and the other string prefixes auto-close in Python, and `"""` closes itself.
- **File types:**
  - `Pipfile`, `poetry.lock`, `uv.lock` and `pdm.lock` open as TOML; `Pipfile.lock` and `.ipynb` as JSON.
  - `uv run`, `pipx run`, `pypy` and free-threaded `python3.14t` shebangs are Python.
  - Toggle Comment in an INI file uses the comment character the file already uses.
- **Java Debug builds the project first.** A Maven or Gradle debug launch asks the Java language server to build
  the project; compile errors stop the launch and are listed in the Debug console as links. Before, Debug ran
  whatever was in `target/classes` (ClassNotFoundException on a new project, old code after an edit).
- **Debug ▶ and Debug on a file use the class's run configuration** (arguments, VM options, environment, working
  directory, JDK), as Run ▶ does, and every unsaved Java file of the project is saved before a Java debug launch.
- **The Debug window never takes the keyboard.** Starting a session or stopping at a breakpoint leaves focus in the
  editor; a stop reopens a closed Debug window. In the Debug window, Stop and Restart need Shift (Shift+K, Shift+R).
- **The stopped line is easy to see:** amber with a gutter arrow, never hidden under the sticky header; the line an
  exception was thrown from is red, and the exception is the top row of Variables.
- **Inline values** stop at the stopped line, and a lambda parameter no longer shows an outer variable's value.
  Hover waits for the mouse to rest and skips comments and strings.
- **Breakpoint kinds differ by shape** (a diamond for a logpoint, "=" marks for a condition), and their hover says
  the condition, log message and hit count. A breakpoint on a blank or comment-only line is refused.
- **Debug window:** opens taller, Variables is the widest column, JVM housekeeping threads are hidden and the
  stopped thread is marked, lambda frames read `<lambda>`, frames without source are muted, stack-trace links
  open on one click, "Exited with code N" stays after the program ends, and setup messages say which piece is
  missing (LSP off, Java server off, jdtls or java-debug missing), with an Install button on the Java card.
- **Debug Test and Debug via Build** use a free JDWP port for Maven test JVMs and Spring Boot, attach every forked
  JVM in turn, and Stop ends the test or build run too.
- **Before-launch steps** of a Java run configuration run in the project root (Run and Debug).
- **Settings schema 129** adds the hot code replace, step filter, static fields and exception class settings;
  workspace schema 19 keeps the exception toggles per project.
- **Mute Breakpoints is kept per project**, fades every breakpoint glyph while on, and is checked in the Run menu.
  Workspace schema 20.
- **Gradle Debug Test and Debug via Build** give every forked JVM a free debug port (through an init script) instead
  of `--debug-jvm`'s fixed 5005, and attach each one in turn.
- **Syntax highlighting for C#, CSS, dotenv, PowerShell and SQL is updated** to the shiki tm-grammars 1.32.22
  grammars (from 1.31.15).
  - CSS colours nested rules (`&`, `> h2` inside a rule), `@layer` name lists, `@import … layer(…)` and the
    operators inside `calc()`.
  - C# knows `union` declarations and the `#:ref` directive of file-based apps, and an interpolation that opens
    at the end of a line no longer ends the string.
  - SQL colours a `[bracketed identifier]` and its `]]` escape; a numeric dotenv value (`PORT=8080`) is a number.
  - PowerShell colours automatic variables (`$Error`, `$Host`, `$PSHome`…) as variables, not constants.
- **IBM Plex Mono is updated from 2.3 to 2.5.** The ASCII control pictures (␀ ␉ ␊ ␛, U+2400–2421) now come from
  Plex itself instead of a fallback font, so they keep the editor's column width, and Plex covers more
  transliteration letters and combining marks. The four font files add about 145 KB to the package.

- **Remote: one login per connect.** Connecting to a remote folder from another window no longer logs in a
  second time for the project's own window: that window takes over the session you just logged in with. A
  password or passphrase is asked for once, and a server that wants a one-time 2FA code no longer needs two of
  them. Closing the window you connected from leaves the project's window connected.
- **Settings switches that only change the editor view** (line numbers, minimap, rulers, wrapping, tab size…)
  no longer rebuild the rest of every window; with many files open they apply about five times faster.
- **Reset to Defaults keeps your AI API keys and the Settings Sync connection.** Its question lists what is reset
  and what is kept and names the backup it writes, and Cancel is the default button.
- **Number fields refuse a value out of range** (shown in red with the range) instead of quietly clamping it.
- **Off switches are visible** in every theme, and a disabled switch is grey.
- **Changing the language** shows "Restart Editora to apply" on its row instead of a dialog at every step.
- **The Settings window stays where you put it** for the rest of the session, and says once that changes apply as
  you make them.
- **Beta pages** carry one Beta pill beside the page title; Settings text grows with the app's font size.
- **List editors apply as you type.** Snippets, Templates, Abbreviations, External Tools and Remote sites no longer
  have a Save button; every change is saved as you make it, as on every other page. Macros keeps Save / Revert.
- **Deleting asks first** on every list editor ("Delete “x”?", Cancel is the default). Removing a Remote site also
  offers to forget that commands may run on its host.
- **Settings that depend on a switch grey out while it is off**, with a note naming the switch, on every page (AI,
  AI Agent, LSP, Debugging, Mermaid, Diagrams, Typst, Git, Remote, Spell Check, rulers, plugins).
- **Bad input is shown, not thrown away.** A ruler list, a TODO pattern, a Remote port or host, a plugin registry
  URL or a sync branch that cannot be used turns its field red with the reason and keeps what you typed.
- **The Editor page is regrouped** into Display, Editing and Clipboard, with Saving right after Indentation; the LSP
  switches on Code Completion are titled "Language server features". Updates and Trusted folders moved to Advanced.
- **Every page has a one-line subtitle**, and help text names the pages that really exist.
- **Shortcuts recorded in Settings show in the active keymap's notation**, in the recorder, the conflict question and
  the status line. A bare letter is refused as the first key of a shortcut.
- **Macro, external-tool and run-configuration shortcuts follow a keymap switch.** Other custom shortcuts are kept
  per keymap, and the Keymap row and "Reset all shortcuts" say so.
- **Snippets can be added for every language**, and snippet and template bodies use Emacs keys only under the Emacs
  keymap.
- **The font list** drops weight variants and math/symbol fonts and marks the bundled fonts; themes are tagged
  (light) or (dark).
- **Simple UI mode trims the right-click menus too**, as it already trimmed the menu bar.
  - **Tab menu:** keeps Save, Save As, Print, Export to PDF, Close, Close Others, Close All, Reveal in File
    Manager, Copy Path and Rename. Unpin stays on a tab that was pinned before.
  - **Editor menu:** keeps Comment / Uncomment, the spelling suggestions, Cut, Copy, Paste, Undo, Redo, Select
    All, Print and Export to PDF. Run, Debug, the LSP, build, AI, Markdown and Typst submenus, Add Bookmark and
    Add Personal Note are hidden.
  - **Project tree menu:** keeps New (a file or a folder), Rename, Undo Move, Delete and Reveal in File
    Manager.
  - **Preview menu** (Markdown, Typst, Markwhen, diagrams): keeps the copy actions, Go to Source, Enlarge,
    Export to PDF and Print. Copy HTML and the Word, OpenDocument, PNG, SVG and Markwhen JSON exports are
    hidden.
  - Git, Local History, the compare actions, Open Terminal, Pin and the bookmark and note entries are hidden
    on the tab, editor and Project tree menus. Turning Simple mode off brings every entry back.

- **HTTP Client: the response view gives the body the room.** The Request, Tests, warnings and headers used to
  stack above the body, which a normal Split left three lines. Now one header row and a tab strip come first.
  - **One header row:** Run (with its shortcut from your keymap), the status as a coloured pill (green 2xx, blue
    3xx, amber 4xx, red 5xx and failures), the time and size, then History. Its tooltip has the full
    status line and when the request was sent.
  - **Tabs:** Body · Headers · Tests · Request · Notes, with counts: the number of headers, tests passed of total
    (red when one failed), and warnings plus files written (amber when there is a warning). Body is shown by
    default. A run switches to Tests on its own only when a test or a script failed; warnings never switch tabs.
    The tab you pick stays across runs while a response has it. Tab reaches the tabs, and the arrow keys, Home and
    End move between them.
  - **Headers** are a name/value list: right-click to copy a value, a header, or all of them. **Request** shows
    the request as sent, highlighted like a `.http` file and filling the tab.
  - **The actions are icons** at the end of the tab strip (Wrap, Copy as cURL, Open in tab, Save response), with
    their shortcuts in the tooltips; Clear is in the **⋯** menu.
  - In a narrow panel History narrows first, then the time and size hide, then History moves to a
    second row. The icons fold into the ⋯ menu, then the counted tabs show only their counts.

- **HTTP Client: the environment is chosen beside the editor.** A `.http` file shows its environment on a pill
  beside the Editor/Split/Preview toggle ("Env: dev", or "No environment"), in every view mode and as soon as the
  file opens, and in the status bar. Clicking either opens the file's environments; `HTTP: Select Environment`
  opens the same menu from the keyboard (arrow keys and Enter; Escape goes back to the editor). The first run of a
  file no longer goes out without an environment because the response view was not open yet. The Environment
  picker in the response view is gone; each file keeps the environment it had.
  - **Use environment dev:** an unresolved `{{variable}}` that an environment of the file defines offers that
    environment as a quick fix — right-click it, or use the Code Actions chord with the caret on it. Its tooltip
    names the fix, and with another environment selected it says which ones define the variable.
  - A variable sent empty is reported with the environments that define it. Each response in History records
    the environment it was sent in, and the response view shows it beside the time and size ("env dev").
  - The menu says when no `http-client.env.json` was found for the file, and opens the env files it has.

  - In a narrow panel History narrows first, then the time and size hide, then History and the environment move
    to a second row. The icons fold into the ⋯ menu, then the counted tabs show only their counts.
- **HTTP Client: the response view says what is going on between responses.**
  - **Before the first run** (and after Clear) it shows which request Run will send — the one at the caret, by its
    `###` title — your Run shortcut, that the gutter's ▶ runs a request, and the file's requests: click one (or
    press Enter on it) to run it.
  - **While a request is sent**, the status says "Sending Get one user… 1.2 s" ("Sending 3 of 10: …" in a Run
    All) over a thin progress line, and the response shown before is one "Previous: 200 OK · 16:42:31 · getUser"
    row, which you can click to see it. Its body no longer disappears without a trace, nor shows under the new
    run.
  - **While a trust prompt is open** it says "Waiting for your answer…" without a clock; the time counts from
    when the request is sent.
  - **After Cancel** it says how long the request ran, and the previous response's row comes back, selected in
    History.
  - **A request that got no response** shows a card in the Body tab naming what went wrong (Connection refused,
    Host not found, Timed out, Certificate problem, Not sent…) with the explanation and Run again and Copy as
    cURL buttons; a pre-request script that did not run also offers its output. The view opens on that card.

- **HTTP Client: response bodies read like other tools show them.** JSON is laid out as `"id": 42`, two spaces
  per level, every field and array element on its own line, and `[]`/`{}` for empty ones (it was Jackson's
  `"id" : 42` with `[ {` on one line). HTML responses, such as a one-line 404 page, are indented one element per
  line, with text and inline tags kept together and the contents of `<pre>`, `<script>`, `<style>`,
  `<textarea>` and comments left as they are; a page the server already indented, or one too irregular to
  format safely, is shown as received. Only the view changes: Save response and Open in tab still write the
  body exactly as it arrived.

- **HTTP Client: image responses say what they are.** A caption line gives the format, the size in pixels and
  the size in bytes ("PNG · 160 × 160 · 858 B"), the picture sits on a checkerboard so transparent parts show,
  and **Fit** (the default, which scales a large picture down to the panel's width but never enlarges a small
  one) and **100%** switch between fitting and the actual size.

### Fixed

- **File Information and the status bar show the same word count.** File Information counted "well-known" and
  "repo's" as two words each and skipped numbers; it now counts as the status bar does.
- **Debugging a Kotlin script with Kotlin 2.4.10:** once the script had run, adding or removing a breakpoint failed
  with "Internal error". Two classes in that compiler carry source-map data (an SMAP) the JDK's debugger cannot
  read; the JVM debugger now treats such a class as one without source information, in breakpoints and in the
  call stack, instead of failing.
- **JavaScript editing without a language server:**
  - JSX in a `.js` file no longer turns the rest of the file into a comment or string (`.js` uses the TSX grammar,
    as VS Code does), and JavaScript is in the status-bar language picker.
  - A regex such as `/`/` or `/\{/` no longer removes every fold, sticky-scroll header and Structure entry below it.
  - Structure lists one-line methods and arrow functions; Go to Symbol finds class and object methods and
    `exports.x =`; Go to Definition picks the nearest declaration; `$` and `#` are part of names.
  - Enter continues a `/** */` comment; Toggle Comment never touches a `#!` shebang and lines its markers up.
  - Smart indent handles `case` bodies, brace-less `if`/`for`/`while`, open argument lists and call chains (in every
    brace language).
  - A quote typed inside a string, comment or regex is not paired.
  - Template literals, `.length`, `import.meta` and BigInt literals get the right colours.
  - `npx`/`pnpm exec`/`bunx` and `zx` shebangs and React modelines are recognised; `.mocharc`, `.nycrc`,
    `.lintstagedrc` and similar open as JSON.
- **A minified file with many long lines no longer stalls highlighting** in every JavaScript tab for about 45 s: it
  opens in long-line mode, and the tokenizer gives long lines a time budget. Typing in a one-line bundle is about 30%
  faster.
- **The TypeScript / JavaScript language server did not start on a fresh install.** npm's latest TypeScript is now
  7, which has no tsserver; Editora's install step (and the Node.js TypeScript Project template) now take
  TypeScript 6. When no usable TypeScript is found the server is not started and the message says why, instead of
  three crashes and "keeps crashing"; Doctor and Settings no longer show it as OK, and opening more tabs no longer
  starts it again.
- **An untrusted folder's own `node_modules/typescript` no longer runs** when a JS/TS file opens: the TypeScript
  installed beside the server is used until the folder is trusted, and the trust prompt lists the folder's copy.
- **The TypeScript server no longer downloads type definitions silently** (`npm install` against the registry into
  `~/.cache/typescript`), and loose scripts in different folders share one server (about 320 MB instead of 550 MB
  each).
- **Organize Imports works on JavaScript and TypeScript**, and the code-action menu offers Fix all, Add missing
  imports and Remove unused. Quick fixes follow the file's indentation. A monorepo without a project open roots at
  its tsconfig/jsconfig.
- **Debugging JavaScript:** `process.stdout.write` / `process.stderr.write` output and `readline` prompts reach the
  Debug console, and the program reads typed input; the program runs from its package folder; node-internal frames
  are skipped; errors in the console and watches say what went wrong instead of "Unset error message."; a js-debug
  that cannot start (or a Node older than 18) says so instead of stopping silently; function values take one line;
  a bad breakpoint condition marks the breakpoint as rejected, once; child processes and workers list all their
  threads; js-debug is pinned to v1.117.0.
- **`node_modules` no longer floods search.** Find in Files, the symbol index, Go to File, Search Everywhere, TODO
  and the Project filter skip `node_modules` even without a `.gitignore` (a 60,000-file `node_modules` used to push
  every project file out of the index); `!node_modules/` in a `.gitignore`, or an include glob naming it, looks
  inside. Find in Files also says when it stopped at its 5,000-match limit exactly at a file boundary.
- **Run console after a flood:** the newest output on screen no longer has gaps when a program printed faster than
  the console could show, and the status line says when output was skipped.
- **npm scripts:** a workspace member runs its workspace's package manager (pnpm, yarn, bun), not npm; an npm run
  configuration uses the project's manager too, and the npm command setting no longer replaces a different manager.
  Settings → Build Tools names the detected manager and why ("pnpm (pnpm-lock.yaml)"). A file inside
  `node_modules` no longer turns the npm tool window into the dependency's. A missing node, npm, pnpm, yarn or bun
  says how to get it instead of showing the Java error; a script that fails with no `node_modules` suggests
  installing first. The Output console draws colours, names the runtime ("Node.js 24.18.1"), and its tab is named
  after the manager. Stop sends Ctrl+C (SIGINT) first to Node and its package managers. A malformed package.json
  says where. Script rows show their command.
- **Test Results with TAP:** a `describe` block is no longer counted as a failed test, and a failure shows its error
  and stack instead of the YAML block.
- **Node.js stack-trace links** work for ESM `file://` frames (spaces, Windows drives), paths with spaces,
  `.jsx/.tsx/.mts/.cts` files and tsc errors, and jump to the column.
- **Run and Output consoles** say when the oldest output was dropped to stay under the size cap.
- **Closing a window no longer keeps it in memory** (about 21 MB each, plugin panes included): the Settings Sync
  listener of every closed window was never removed.
- **A plugin thread can no longer keep Editora running after quit**, where the next launch was "handed to" an
  editor with no window.
- **Chords a plugin bound in code survive a keymap switch or a key-binding edit**, and a keymap rebuild in Simple
  mode no longer turns plugin chords on.
- **A plugin's `start()` is timed**; one that holds up window opening is named.
- **Registry and download reads have an overall deadline**, a second Browse while one is fetching joins it, a picked
  file over the size cap is refused before it is read, and an install worker that fails always reports back.
- **Removing a plugin deletes its plugin.json last**, so a folder that cannot be fully deleted stays listed and
  removable; staging folders a crash left behind are swept at start; concurrent rescans can no longer close class
  loaders in use.
- **Plugin versions compare by semver**: `rc10 > rc2`, `+build` is ignored, `v2.0 < 10.0`; the install question
  says Update, Reinstall or Downgrade where that is what an install would do, and Browse marks a newer installed
  version.
- **The palette shows plugin chords**, plugin right-click items have their own separator, a plugin status segment is
  reachable by keyboard and names its plugin, and `caretLine()` is right in a narrowed buffer.
- **The minimise, maximise and close buttons were nearly invisible with a dark theme and the menu bar in the
  title bar.** They followed the desktop's light or dark setting rather than Editora's theme, so a dark theme on
  a light desktop drew them dark on dark. They now follow the app theme, and change with it.
- **When the system had no file watcher to give** (Linux: inotify instances used up), the project tree and language
  servers silently stopped following the disk. They now check folders every 2 seconds, and on Windows also notice
  a save that replaces a file with one of the same size and time.
- **Plugins: Set Registry URL** accepted an address that is not https; it now refuses it like the Settings field.
- **A submenu's › arrow sat in the middle of its menu** (VCS → Changes, Branches, …), just past the longest
  submenu name. It now sits at the menu's right edge, past the shortcut column.
- **A Markdown code span after a stray double backtick rendered as plain text** (``` `` `a` `c` ``` showed
  `` `c` `` literally): commonmark-java 0.30.1 fixes the regression 0.30.0 brought in.
- **With a dark UI theme and a light editor theme, the Welcome and Doctor tabs were white blocks** with
  near-invisible titles; their selected tab now takes the page's own background.

- **Spell check accepts the possessive of any dictionary word**, such as "someone else's" and "another's". Only
  words the dictionary lists with a possessive were accepted.
- **Settings scrolled sideways at its 900 px minimum width** in German, French, Spanish and Portuguese (Snippets,
  Templates, Remote), and controls sat a scrollbar's width apart on short and long pages.
- **A `.http` file saved as Markdown kept its `{{variable}}` squiggles** until Markdown lint's first result
  replaced them, and for good with Markdown lint off.
- **A snippet trigger with a space in it was saved and never expanded.** It is now refused with the reason shown.
- **Python:**
  - Run used `python3` from PATH whatever the project or the Debug setting said.
  - Output arrived only when the program ended, with stderr ahead of stdout.
  - On Windows the Store stub ran, and `print('✓')` raised `UnicodeEncodeError`.
  - Changing a Python configuration's working directory broke its target.
  - ▶ on a test file reported exit code 0 without running a test.
- **Python Debug:**
  - Debugging a `multiprocessing` program hung.
  - `input()` raised `EOFError`.
  - An interpreter with arguments or an `env` prefix hung or lost them.
  - A breakpoint the debugger moved onto a conditional one silently dropped its condition.
  - Hovering `p.x` showed the local `x`.
  - A Python row in Test Results had no Debug This Test item.
  - A file with a `uv run --script` (or pipx, Poetry, PDM) shebang handed debugpy the runner instead of a Python;
    Debug runs it under the project's Python.
  - debugpy installed without Node and is no longer fetched again while debugging is off.
- **Python code intelligence:**
  - A new module created outside Editora never resolved until a restart.
  - Windows with no project saw no file changes at all.
  - A nested `requirements.txt` split the project's server.
  - A missing custom server command was offered the Pyright installer.
  - An empty "…" stayed in the status bar.
  - The hover cut off Pyright's signature block.
  - Structure showed return types with a trailing colon.
- **Python console links:**
  - Extensionless scripts, warnings and pytest/mypy/ruff `file.py:12:` lines are now links.
  - So are pdb's `> file.py(12)` lines and paths containing quotes.
- **Python Project template:** its README commands work on a fresh project.
- **Spell check:** it now checks the first word of an f-string. Common Python terms (kwargs, asyncio, noqa) are no
  longer flagged.
- **Go to Symbol without a language server:** Python methods show their class.
- **Java Debug:**
  - A class with a `package` line in a folder with no `pom.xml` or Gradle build could not be debugged
    ("Could not find or load main class Main"). Editora now corrects the Java server's source folder.
  - Debug on a file could run a different program: another `main` of the project, or a class never compiled.
  - Editing a file during a session moved its breakpoints and the stopped line off the code the program runs;
    lines are now matched to the launched code, and a stop in an edited file says the program runs the old code.
  - Breakpoints in other unsaved files were silently not hit.
  - Starting a session moved focus into the Debug window, where typing `r` or `k` restarted or killed the program.
  - With "Run the debugged program in the Debug console" off, a crashed Java language server left the program
    running; a lost connection to the debugger now ends the program at once and says so.
  - A breakpoint set while the session was starting flashed "Empty debug session." as invalid.
  - Run to Cursor ran past a line that had a false conditional breakpoint or a logpoint.
  - Every stop fetched the whole call stack (thousands of frames in deep recursion); it is now paged.
  - Stop and Restart froze the window for up to a quarter of a second, and logged a "Socket closed" stack trace.
  - Hover and inline values showed the wrong variable for `obj.field`.
  - A compile error of a loose file showed only in the status bar; it is now in the Debug console with links.
  - A slow evaluation timed out with a raw Java exception name, and a Step pressed meanwhile fired seconds later.
  - Install Java Support downloaded java-debug again while debugging was off; with `--config-dir` the installed
    plugin was not found.
  - Restart of a run configuration used its old arguments; F5 in another tab stopped a running session without
    asking; Attach, configurations and Debug via Build of a remote file checked this machine's tools instead of
    the host's; remote launch arguments were quoted for this machine's OS.
  - java-debug's "different versions of JVMs" warning no longer clutters the console, and a program java-debug
    started now ends with "The program ended." instead of a made-up exit code 0.
  - Debugger launch, connect and adapter errors were English in every language and could start with Java class
    names (`org.eclipse.debug.core.DebugException: …`); they are now translated and plain, and a report of
    several lines goes to the Debug console with its first line in the status bar.
  - With "Run the debugged program in the Debug console" off, the console now shows the program's real exit code
    (Linux and macOS, programs on this machine); java-debug always reported 0.
  - Emoji and other characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane showed garbled in Java string values (a bug in
    Eclipse's debugger inside jdtls); Variables, watches, hover and inline values now show them as written.

- **"Snippets: Manage", "Sync setup" and the Doctor links opened an empty page** when a search was left in the
  Settings search box.
- **What Settings search found depended on which pages you had opened** before searching.
- **A change in another window wiped text you were typing** in an open Settings window, and every reopen ran
  `git --version`.
- **Shortcut chips in Settings used the editor theme's colours** instead of the app theme's.
- **A multi-line abbreviation was saved flattened** when you clicked into it and out again. The expansion is now a
  multi-line field, and nothing is saved unless you change it.
- **With one saved Remote site, the first edit emptied and greyed out the form.**
- **Escape in a macro's Key step closed Settings** instead of recording Escape.
- **Reset on a shortcut whose default chord another command took did nothing.** It now offers to take the chord back.
- **A blank template Id discarded every other edit in the form.**
- **Two macros could share a name**, and a duplicate abbreviation key (ignoring case) overrode the other silently.
- **"Add pattern" on the TODO page matched every TODO a second time.**
- **The TODO part-colour pickers showed old colours** after Reset or a change made elsewhere.
- **Tool Windows ▲ / ▼ sometimes did nothing visible.**
- **"Rulers by language" accepted names that never matched**, and a mistyped ruler list was silently replaced.
- **"Enable plugins" left every plugin's checkbox greyed** until Reload.
- **A wrong git or gh path said "install git"** and locked the Enable Git switch on.
- **Browse… beside the API key and model fields opened a file chooser.**
- **A server, agent or debugger path with a space in it never started.**
- **The AI status pill stayed "Connected"** after turning AI off.
- **The Markdown page** split the pasted-image rows, had a scroller inside the page, and a blank gap.
- **A broken plugin.json showed the parser's internals**; Browse plugins… hid Settings before the picker opened.
- **Java debug-adapter detection ran on the UI thread.**

- **Remote: an SSH config with a `Match` section no longer stops every connect.** Editora skips `Match`
  sections (it cannot evaluate them) and reads the rest of the file; before, any `Match` made every connect
  fail with "Currently not able to process Match sections".
